subject: On-prem licensing split & critical support path
messages:
From: Elliot Chen <elliot.chen@benedoc.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Aisha Mahajan <aisha.mahajan@benedoc.com>, procurement@benedoc.com
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem licensing split & critical support path

Sergio — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Benedoc is keen to move forward with a private deployment but procurement needs a clearer commercial construct before we can start legal. Two specific asks: 

1) Can you split the commercial into (a) perpetual-style operator licenses per site vs (b) an annual platform fee? We need unit economics to show to our finance team.

2) Our clinical workloads are business-critical. Can you map the support tiers (response times, included oncall, priority queueing) to specific fees and indicate any add-on implementation credits / success SOW credits?

Attached is a high-level SOW for scope context.

Appreciate a short breakdown and a recommended path for a 3-site pilot -> production roll.

Best,
Elliot
Procurement Lead, Benedoc Health

Attachments: Benedoc_SOW_v1.pdf, network_requirements.xlsx

From: sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: Elliot Chen <elliot.chen@benedoc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem licensing split & critical support path

Elliot — thanks for the clear asks and the SOW, this is helpful. High-level proposal below; happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through.

Summary (pilot: 3 sites -> production):
- Operator licenses: flat per-operator node license (site-level) priced as annual renewals; includes runtime entitlements and limited operator console.
- Platform fee: annualized platform fee that covers centralized control plane, updates, and access to Redwood Optimize. This is the primary amortized charge.
- Support tiers: 
  * Standard (P3): 8x5 email + next-business-day response — included with platform fee.
  * Enhanced (P2): 24x7 email + 4-hour business-impact response + quarterly health checks — add-on.
  * Critical (P1): 24x7 phone + 1-hour response SLA, prioritized engineering bridge access — premium add-on.
- Implementation credits: for pilots we can offer up to 10% credit on the implementation SOW if a production commitment (12 months platform fee + min operator commitment) is signed within 60 days of pilot completion.

Rough commercial bands (ballpark, subject to final SOW and site sizing):
- Operator license: $18k / site / year (example: 3 sites = $54k/year)
- Platform fee: $120k / year (pilot SKU; scales with token/throughput expectation)
- Support: Standard included, Enhanced +$36k / year, Critical +$110k / year

Options to reduce upfront cash: (choose one)
A) Defer 50% platform fee to start of production (we keep operator invoices on pilot at reduced rate).
B) Implementation credit (10%) applied as invoice credit upon production sign.

I'll assign Marissa to draft a condensed commercial summary and Kimberly to confirm the SLA wording we'll include in the MSA. Which option would Benedoc prefer for cashflow?

— Sergio
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Sergio — quick technical clarifications from our infra team: 

- The platform fee band will need to accommodate occasional bursts during chart-migration windows. Is there a documented overage or burst policy and cost?
- For Critical support (P1), does the SLA include on-call engineering for redeploys that may require overnight node maintenance? We need guaranteed windows.

If you can confirm wording we can include final language in our redline to legal.

Thanks,
Aisha
Senior Engineering Manager, Benedoc Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Mahajan <aisha.mahajan@benedoc.com>, sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Chen <elliot.chen@benedoc.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem licensing split & critical support path

Aisha — good Qs. Clarifications below and one commercial concession proposal: 

Burst policy: 
- Pilot: included burst up to 2x baseline throughput for up to 48 hours (no charge).
- Production: baseline throughput included in platform fee; bursts billed at $0.035 per extra token-equivalent or via temporary scale-up node at negotiated day-rate. We can add a 3-month burst buffer as a one-time add-on to the platform fee if you want predictable runway.

P1 support scope: 
- Includes 24x7 engineering bridge for P1 incidents and scheduled engineering assistance for emergency redeploys that are incident-driven (max 6 hours per event).
- For non-incident scheduled maintenance (e.g., planned overnight upgrades), P1 includes priority scheduling but may require a short implementation fee for discrete engineering hours beyond the included incident assistance.

Commercial concession proposal (pilot -> production sign within 60 days):
- 12% implementation credit applied as invoice credit (improves over Sergio's 10% ask).
- If Benedoc commits to a 24-month platform fee term at signing, we will cap the Critical support add-on at +$88k/year (instead of $110k).

Sergio / Kimberly — internal approval required to hold the Critical cap and 12% credit. Kimberly, do we need legal to pre-bake the SLA definitions for P1/P2?

Best,
Marissa
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>

Marissa — I can pre-bake SLA language. Quick internal notes: 
- Approve 12% implementation credit for pilot-conversion clause (finance confirmed as conditional credit; requires counter-signed order form).
- Approve Critical cap to $88k/year for 24-month committed term. 
- Confirmed burst buffer add-on wording (3-month buffer) — ops will provide a short blurb to include in the SOW.

I'll draft the P1/P2 definitions and a short MSA-friendly paragraph for the platform fee amortization. Sergio — if you want me to attach for legal intake, say so and I'll push a redline.

Kimberly Park
Director, Contracts & Pricing, Redwood Inference

Team — this is great, thanks. Benedoc preference:

1) Go with the 12% implementation credit and the Critical cap at $88k/year in exchange for a 24-month platform commitment.
2) We'd like the 3-month burst buffer included in year 1 platform fee (to avoid surprises during our migration).

Please prepare a concise commercial summary and an order form we can circulate internally. If legal gets the pre-baked SLA paragraph and a redline-ready MSA, we can move much faster.

I'll expect the commercial summary + draft order form by end of day Thursday so procurement can review Friday morning.

Best,
Elliot
